subject: Energy
title: The Rise of Coal
description: A quick win: understand The Rise of Coal.

hook.text: Coal burning began in China over 3,000 years ago—but it was in 18th-century Britain that coal changed the world.

buildup.text: As England's forests vanished, coal became the replacement fuel—dirtier and harder to extract, but far more abundant.

discovery.text: Coal packs 2–3 times the energy of wood per kilogram—making it a denser, more transportable fuel.

twist.text: Flooded coal mines required pumps—which directly led to the invention of the steam engine by Thomas Newcomen.

climax.text: Coal didn't just fuel industry—it created the conditions that demanded steam power, launching the Industrial Revolution.

punchline.text: Coal replaced wood—and accidentally invented the modern world.

quiz.question: What problem in coal mines led to the steam engine?
